name: Yemisi Shyllon Museum of Art
funding: University museum opened 2019, endowed by collector Prince Yemisi Shyllon; free entry from June 2026 paid by Aisha and Gbenga Oyebode.
watch: On the Pan-Atlantic University campus. Its 2026 free-admission funder chairs a palm-oil firm in a land dispute.
records_note: Annual reports 2020 to 2025 give income shares but no accounts; sponsor logos are undated; the supervisory council and advisory board are named.

name: Bandjoun Station
funding: Small artist-run centre opened 2013, paid for by Barthélémy Toguo, his coffee plantations and the Amis de Bandjoun Station association.
watch: Residencies, museum and farm in the Bamileke highlands; MO.CO Montpellier sends graduates for residencies (since 2023).
records_note: The live site is down; its January 2025 archived copy has no reports, accounts, funder list or board, only project text and press.

name: Les Ateliers Sahm
funding: Small art centre founded 2012 by Bill Kouélany, funded project by project: Fondation Almayuda (since 2018), Institut français, EU/OACPS (Popul'Art 2023).
watch: The only contemporary art centre in this research for the Republic of the Congo. Almayuda is a Geneva foundation registered in 2023.
records_note: No site of its own found, only Facebook; no reports, accounts, funder list or board; funder Almayuda names it on its own site.

name: Musée National du Mali
funding: State museum with 10,937 visitors in 2025, run by Mali's culture ministry; Spain's AECID backs the 2026 'Repenser le Musée' project (amount undisclosed).
watch: EU paid for its 2002 extension. In April 2026 Spain launched a project for training, conservation and outreach.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, funder list or board on the museum's old site; its web address now redirects to an unrelated site.

name: Musée National de Guinée (Sandervalia)
funding: State museum being rebuilt with a €16M concessional AFD (France) loan signed 30 Mar 2026; the Guinean state funds operations.
watch: To become an autonomous public body after an 8,000 m2 extension. This is AFD's first large sovereign loan for Guinean culture.
records_note: No site of its own found; the culture ministry's site has only a March 2026 news item on the AFD loan, nothing else.

name: Musée National du Burkina Faso
funding: State museum (EPSCT) with 30,000+ visits Jan-Oct 2024, funded by the culture ministry plus Ouagadougou commune, Agence Faso Mɛbo and unnamed company donors.
watch: Its director says partners rarely back museums. A friends' association started a donation drive in April 2026.
records_note: Documents page is empty and no accounts or funders are posted; the site says a board exists under a 2002 decree but names no one.

name: Le Cube – independent art room
funding: Small artist-run space founded 2005 by Elisabeth Piskernik; residencies paid by artists, partners are foreign cultural institutes and embassies.
watch: Independent exhibition and residency space at 2 rue Benzerte, with a Vienna branch; still programming in 2026.
records_note: Le Cube names partners only for single exhibitions and publishes no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Musée Mohammed VI d'Art Moderne et Contemporain (MMVI)
funding: State museum run since 2014 by the Fondation Nationale des Musées, built with Ministry of Culture and Fonds Hassan II money; partners include Royal Air Maroc.
watch: Morocco's first national museum of modern and contemporary art, opened October 2014 by the king; FNM president Mehdi Qotbi.
records_note: The museum has no site of its own; its parent foundation FNM publishes no annual reports, accounts or funder list and names no board.

name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech
funding: Opened 2017, paid for by Pierre Bergé's 2015 sale of Moroccan art and run on Jardin Majorelle ticket income (700k+ visitors a year); a luxury-fashion legacy.
watch: Run by the Fondation Jardin Majorelle (president Madison Cox) next to the garden; it shares the site's 700k+ visitors.
records_note: The museum site and the Jardin Majorelle site publish no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; the parent foundation's own site returned unreadable code.

name: Musée Public National d'Art Moderne et Contemporain (MAMA)
funding: Public body (EPA) under the Ministry of Culture since 2007, with little budget beyond its opening; collection built mostly from private and artist donations.
watch: In a 1909 neo-Moorish department store on rue Larbi Ben M'hidi; opened for Algiers Capital of Arab Culture 2007.
records_note: Its old site, now offline, showed no reports, accounts, funder list or board in an archived copy; only mission, publications and a support link.

name: Darb 1718 Contemporary Art and Culture Center
funding: Small non-profit founded 2008 and mainly funded by artist Moataz Nasr; 2022 Moleskine Foundation grant; 2025 artist-donated auction at Tarathuna.
watch: Fustat headquarters bulldozed in January 2024; working from temporary space and raising money for a new home.
records_note: The live site is suspended; its archived copy has no reports or accounts, shows six unlabelled collaborator logos with no date, and lists no board.

name: B7L9 Art Centre (Kamel Lazaar Foundation)
funding: Opened 2019, funded by the Kamel Lazaar Foundation (money from Swicorp, a banking firm); partners include the EU, the German Foreign Office, Goethe, Pro Helvetia, Tunisair and Porticus.
watch: Tunisia's first non-profit contemporary art centre, in the Bhar Lazreg suburb; replaces B'chira Art Center, which has no recent record.
